label: v1.1-draft
description: DRAFT v1.1: clarifies the two SDF audit controls as data audit, following S.O. 5458(E) (2026), and annotates Rule 4 commencement under Rule 1(3), as corrected by G.S.R. 892(E). Rule 4 date annotations do not determine the commencement of linked Act provisions or automatically change applicability/scoring. Qualified legal review is still required before reliance.

sections.title: Sec 8 - General Obligations of Data Fiduciary
Sec 9 - Children and Persons with Disability
Sec 18-28 - Data Protection Board of India

controls.title: Determine whether each processing activity is covered by the Act: digital personal data, or non-digital data later digitised, processed in India
Identify processing outside India that is connected with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India
Confirm which data falls outside the Act: personal or domestic use, and data made public by the Data Principal or under a legal obligation
Keep a dated record of the applicability assessment and revisit it when products, markets or data flows change
Process personal data only for a lawful purpose, and only with the Data Principal's consent or for a Sec 7 legitimate use
Check that no stated purpose is expressly forbidden by law
Record the ground (consent, or the specific Sec 7 limb) for every processing activity in the RoPA
Give the Data Principal a notice with, or before, every request for consent
Notice itemises the personal data to be processed and the specific purpose
Notice explains how to withdraw consent and how to use the grievance redressal route
Notice explains how to make a complaint to the Board
Notice is in clear, plain language and stands on its own instead of being buried in other terms
Notice gives an itemised description of the goods, services or uses that the processing enables
Notice gives a working link or other means to withdraw consent and exercise rights
Notice is available in English or any Eighth Schedule language on request
For consent given before the Act commenced, send a notice as soon as practicable and continue processing only until consent is withdrawn
Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action
Consent covers only the personal data necessary for the specified purpose
Every consent request is accompanied or preceded by the notice
Consent request is available in English or any Eighth Schedule language
Consent request gives the contact details of the DPO or designated person
No consent term is relied on if it limits rights or breaches the Act; such a term is not binding
Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it
Withdrawal does not undo earlier lawful processing, and the Data Principal bears the consequences of withdrawing
On withdrawal, processing stops and Data Processors are made to stop within a reasonable time, unless law requires retention
Records exist to prove that notice was given and consent obtained
Consent Managers register with the Board as an Indian company meeting the prescribed conditions

controls.title: Sec 7(a): where data was voluntarily provided for a specified purpose with no objection, use it only for that purpose
Sec 7(b): State subsidy, benefit, service, certificate or licence is processed only within the notified standards
Sec 7(c): performance of State functions, or processing for sovereignty, integrity or security, is tied to a law
Sec 7(d): disclosure required by law is limited to what the legal obligation demands
Sec 7(e): processing to comply with a judgment, decree or order is documented against that order
Sec 7(f): processing in a medical emergency threatening life is limited to the emergency and recorded
Sec 7(g): processing during an epidemic or public-health threat is limited to the response
Sec 7(h): processing during a disaster or breakdown of public order is limited to the assistance or safety measures needed
Sec 7(i): processing for employment, or to protect the employer from loss or liability, is documented and proportionate
The Data Fiduciary is accountable for compliance, including for processing done by its Data Processors
Data Processors are engaged only under a valid written contract
Processor contracts set the purpose, safeguards, breach duties and control over sub-processors
Data is kept complete, accurate and consistent where it drives decisions about a Data Principal or is shared with another fiduciary
Technical and organisational measures are in place to ensure the Act is observed effectively
Reasonable security safeguards protect personal data in your possession or under your control from breach
Personal data is encrypted, obfuscated or masked, or replaced with virtual tokens
Access to systems and personal data is controlled and limited to those who need it
Logging, monitoring and review give visibility to detect unauthorised access and to investigate it
Backups and continuity measures let you recover data after loss, destruction or compromise
Logs and relevant personal data are kept for at least one year to detect, investigate and remedy
Contracts with Data Processors require them to apply the same safeguards
Technical and organisational measures for effective observance of the safeguards are documented and reviewed
A breach response process exists and Data Processors must report breaches to the Data Fiduciary
Each affected Data Principal is told of a breach without delay: what happened, the likely harm, steps taken, steps they can take, and a contact
The Board is told of a breach without delay, with a detailed report within 72 hours
Personal data is erased, and Data Processors are made to erase it, once consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served, unless law requires retention
Where the Rules require it, personal data, traffic data and logs are retained for the minimum period
For the classes of fiduciary named in the Rules, data is erased after the prescribed inactivity period and the Data Principal is warned beforehand
Business contact details of the DPO or designated person are published
A grievance redressal mechanism exists and responses are given inside the prescribed period
Data Principals are directed to the grievance mechanism first, before they approach the Board
Verifiable consent of a parent or lawful guardian is obtained before processing a child's personal data
Verifiable consent of the lawful guardian is obtained before processing the data of a person with a disability who cannot decide for themselves
Due diligence checks that the person giving consent is an identifiable adult who is the child's parent or guardian
No processing is carried out that is likely to harm a child's well-being
No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising is directed at children, subject to the notified exemptions
Where an exemption for a class of fiduciary or purpose is relied on, the class and conditions are documented
Assess whether the organisation could be notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, based on volume and sensitivity of data and risk to Data Principals
Appoint a DPO based in India who answers to the Board or similar governing body and is the point of contact for grievances
Appoint an independent data auditor to evaluate compliance
Carry out periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments
Carry out periodic data audits and take other measures required by the Act
Complete the DPIA and data audit every 12 months and give the Board a report of significant observations
Verify that algorithmic software used on personal data does not put Data Principals at risk, and apply any data localisation the Government specifies
Data Principals can get a summary of their personal data and the processing carried out
Data Principals can learn who their data has been shared with and what was shared
Data Principals can have inaccurate or misleading data corrected, incomplete data completed, and data updated
Data Principals can have data erased unless retention is needed for the purpose or by law
Readily available grievance redressal means exist, and a response is given within the prescribed period
Data Principals can nominate another person to exercise their rights on death or incapacity
Communications remind Data Principals to comply with applicable laws when exercising their rights
Identity is checked so nobody can impersonate another person when providing or changing data
A defined procedure handles false or frivolous grievances and complaints
Correction and erasure requests are accepted only with verifiably authentic information
Transfers of personal data outside India are checked against the countries the Government has restricted
Any sector law that gives stronger protection or tighter transfer limits is identified and followed
Where rights and duties are set aside to enforce a legal right or claim, the reliance is documented
Processing by courts, tribunals and regulators for judicial or regulatory functions is identified
Processing to prevent, detect, investigate or prosecute offences is documented against the exemption
Where an Indian processor handles data of people outside India under a foreign contract, the exemption and its limits are recorded
Processing under an approved merger, demerger or similar arrangement is documented
Processing to ascertain the financial position, assets or liabilities of a defaulter is documented
Processing for research, archiving or statistics follows the prescribed standards and is not used to decide about an individual
If the organisation falls under a notified start-up or class exemption, the notification and its scope are recorded
Name a person who receives and answers Board notices, directions and requests
Be able to produce records and information the Board may require during an inquiry
Carry out Board directions on urgent remedial or mitigation measures after a breach
A process exists to answer Data Principal complaints that reach the Board
The team can engage with the Board's digital process for filings, hearings and orders
A process exists to appeal a Board order to the Appellate Tribunal within the time limit
Board directions and decisions are logged and their compliance tracked
Appellate Tribunal orders are complied with, and relevant records are preserved while an appeal is open
Policy exists on using mediation or other dispute resolution when the Board proposes it
Policy exists for deciding when to offer a voluntary undertaking to the Board, and for honouring one
A penalty exposure register maps obligations to the Schedule's penalty bands
Evidence of mitigation, remediation and good faith is kept, because the Board weighs it when setting a penalty
The organisation can respond to a Board inquiry, which must be held before any penalty is imposed
The Board or governing body receives periodic reporting on DPDPA exposure and remediation progress
